prompt: The sidecar fetched the shop's page from `localhost:8080`. Why does `localhost` reach the shop?
hint: What do the containers of one pod share?

choices.text: kube-proxy forwards localhost to the pod's Service
choices.why: There is no Service here at all; kube-proxy is not involved.

choices.text: They share one network namespace
choices.why: Right. One interface, one address, one localhost for every container of the pod.

choices.text: The sidecar runs inside the shop's container
choices.why: They are separate containers, from separate images; only the namespaces are shared.

choices.text: The emptyDir volume carries the requests
choices.why: The volume holds files; the request went over the network, to localhost.

prompt: `kubectl get pod web` showed `READY 2/2` for a pod with three containers. Why two?
hint: One of them is not supposed to be running.

choices.text: One container failed to start
choices.why: The pod was `Running` with no restarts; nothing had failed.

choices.text: The sidecar is not counted because it has no port
choices.why: Ports have nothing to do with the count; the sidecar is one of the two.

choices.text: The init container had already finished, and only running ones are counted
choices.why: Right. Its own status said `Completed`.

choices.text: Pods count containers per node, and two fit on that node
choices.why: All containers of a pod are on the same node; the count is of the pod's containers.

prompt: A team wants to put their web application and its PostgreSQL in one pod, 'so they are always together'. What is the best objection?
hint: Ask whether they must live and die together.

choices.text: A pod cannot hold more than two containers
choices.why: This lesson's pod held three.

choices.text: PostgreSQL cannot listen on localhost
choices.why: It can; a shared localhost is not the problem.

choices.text: Two containers of a pod run on different nodes
choices.why: A pod's containers always run on the same node.

choices.text: They scale, fail and update differently
choices.why: Right. Three copies of the application would mean three databases; they belong in two controllers.

prompt: After the sidecar was stopped from the node, what did `kubectl get pod web` show?
hint: Look at RESTARTS and AGE together.

choices.text: The same pod, with one restart
choices.why: Right: `RESTARTS 1 (8s ago)`, and the age kept counting from the pod's creation.

choices.text: A new pod with a new name and address
choices.why: A container restart keeps the pod; only a deleted pod is replaced.

choices.text: The pod `Pending` until the scheduler placed it again
choices.why: The kubelet restarts the container where it is; the scheduler is not asked.

choices.text: The pod `Completed`, since one container had exited
choices.why: With `restartPolicy: Always` an exit is a restart, not an end.

prompt: Match each `restartPolicy` with what happens when a container exits.
A container keeps crashing a second after it starts. What does the kubelet do over time?
hint: The pod's status gets a name for the waiting.

choices.text: Restarts it as fast as it can, forever
choices.why: It waits longer each time, up to five minutes.

choices.text: Gives up after three attempts and deletes the pod
choices.why: The kubelet never deletes the pod; it keeps trying with longer waits.

choices.text: Waits longer before each restart, showing `CrashLoopBackOff`
choices.why: Right: ten seconds, twenty, forty, up to five minutes.

choices.text: Moves the pod to a healthier node
choices.why: The kubelet only acts on its own node; it cannot move anything.

prompt: Ana deleted the bare pod `web`. What made it different from deleting a pod of a Deployment?

choices.text: A bare pod cannot be deleted while running
choices.why: It was deleted while running; the command succeeded.

choices.text: Its containers kept running on the node without a pod
choices.why: Deleting a pod stops its containers.

choices.text: No controller noticed, so nothing replaced it
choices.why: Right: `No resources found`. Nobody had promised that the pod would exist.

choices.text: It was moved to the `kube-system` namespace
choices.why: Deleted objects are not moved anywhere.

prompt: Which of these does a container lose when the kubelet restarts it in the same pod? Choose all that apply.
hint: What belongs to the container, and what to the pod?

choices.text: Files it wrote to its own filesystem
choices.why: Right: a restarted container starts from its image again.

choices.text: The pod's IP address
choices.why: The address belongs to the pod and stays.

choices.text: Files in the pod's emptyDir
choices.why: The emptyDir belongs to the pod and survives the restart.

choices.text: What it held in memory
choices.why: Right: it is a new process.

choices.text: The pod's name
choices.why: The pod is the same object, so its name is too.

prompt: Put the life of this lesson's pod in order.
hint: The init container comes before anything else runs.
items: The pod is scheduled onto a node
The init container writes the greeting and exits
The shop and the sidecar start side by side
The sidecar is stopped and the kubelet restarts it
The pod is deleted and nothing replaces it
trap: Containers in `containers` only start once every init container has finished, and nothing comes after the deletion of a bare pod.
